title: Resolve the dichotomy: construct a YES witness OR prove a NO no-go theorem (Q1.2 currently unanswered)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Open dichotomy not addressed: is Question 1.2 even answerable YES? Consider a no-go theorem.**

The current `solution.tex` proves its only concrete candidate $\A$ (Definition `def:A`) **fails** the negative clause (P2) (Lemma `lem:leak`, Cor. `cor:P2-fails`), and closes by leaving the actual construction "as the outstanding task." So *no* witnessing structure exists in the attempt, and Question 1.2 is unanswered.

Crucially, the draft's Remark `rem:spec` argues only **heuristically** that (P1) and (P2) are "in genuine tension":

> any mechanism that propagates orientation from finitely many anchored gadgets to all gadgets (needed for (i)/(P1) with a uniform shift) is equally available to the adversary's existential formulas (defeating (ii)/(P2)).

This is presented as informal motivation, not a theorem. It leaves a genuine **dichotomy unresolved**, and a solver should pursue *both* branches in parallel:

**(B1) YES branch.** Build a single computably-represented $\B$ with $\AUT(\B)$ countable such that
- (P1) every $\pi\in\AUT(\B)$ is $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from *some* finite tuple; and
- (P2) for every finite $\bar a$, some $\pi\in\AUT(\B)$ is not $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definable from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ — via the embedding criterion `lem:embcrit`: a self-embedding $h$ of $\B$ (global, preserving+reflecting **all** relations) fixing $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ pointwise with $h\pi\neq\pi h$.

This requires decoupling *coordination* (needed for countability) from *orientation transmission* (which kills P2). The spine+anchor of `def:A` does the opposite and is provably fatal.

**(B2) NO branch (currently entirely unconsidered).** Prove a no-go theorem: that every countable structure with countable automorphism group that is computably $\AUT$-countable on a cone admits, for some fixed finite $\bar a$, a uniform $\Sigma^{in}_1$-definition of every automorphism from $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$ — i.e. the naive effectivization of Theorem 2.2 cannot be defeated. If true, the answer to Question 1.2 is NO, and Remark `rem:spec`'s "tension" upgrades to a proof.

**Why this matters / why it is hard.** The draft has correctly: (i) fixed the abstract negative-clause criterion (embedding preservation of $\exists$-formulas, sound), and (ii) diagnosed the orientation-leak trap. But it has *not* established that the YES branch is achievable at all, nor ruled it out. The countability constraint ($(\Z/2)^{\N}$ is uncountable, so per-gadget choices must be collapsed) is in direct opposition to keeping per-gadget data existentially invisible — this is the crux and the content of the Thm 2.2 / Thm 2.3 gap.

**Concrete next steps.**
1. Attempt the YES construction with an *undirected*/parity coupling (no directed spine an $\exists$-witness can traverse to read an absolute orientation), so that the local reflection $\rho$ extends to a **global** self-embedding fixing any external tuple.
2. Alternatively code a non-c.e.-on-a-cone set $X$ (per prob-01-5) on gadgets above $\max$ index touched by $\bar a\cup\pi(\bar a)$, and check (P1) survives.
3. In parallel, attempt to convert Remark `rem:spec`'s tension into a no-go theorem (B2).
